stories.title: Personalized mRNA neoantigen therapy improves recurrence-free survival in Phase 3 melanoma trial
stories.takeaway: In the randomized INTerpath-001 study, individualized intismeran autogene plus pembrolizumab reduced the relative risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 42% versus pembrolizumab alone after surgery.
stories.what_happened: Merck and Moderna released detailed results on October 22 from 1,137 patients with completely resected stage IIB–IV melanoma. At a median 24.6-month follow-up, two-year recurrence-free survival was 82.2% with the combination versus 70.0% with pembrolizumab alone (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.45–0.75). Distant-metastasis-free survival also improved; the results were scheduled for presentation at ESMO 2026.
stories.why_it_matters: A pivotal clinical test of patient-specific mRNA manufacturing and neoantigen immunotherapy, with implications for precision biotechnology and translational platform development.
stories.caveat: The therapy remains investigational; overall-survival data are immature, benefit in other cancers is unproven, and the report is a company-released trial readout rather than an independently evaluated full publication.

stories.title: Microbiota-derived butyrate intersects with non-enzymatic IDO1 signaling in cardiac injury
stories.takeaway: A new mouse study links reduced gut-microbiota-derived butyrate with cardiac oxidative injury through a STAT1–IDO1–ANGPTL4 pathway, including a signaling function of IDO1 distinct from its enzymatic activity.
stories.what_happened: Published October 25 in Cell Death & Disease, Liu and colleagues used angiotensin II-treated mice and molecular perturbations to show that IDO1 Y111 phosphorylation engages SHP2 and relieves Notch1/HES1 repression, increasing ANGPTL4-associated oxidative damage. Butyrate acted through AHR/SOCS3-linked regulation and IDO1 degradation in the experimental system.
stories.why_it_matters: Illustrates how microbial metabolites can regulate host tissue signaling and redox responses beyond the intestine, motivating more mechanistically resolved host–microbe research.
stories.caveat: Primarily mechanistic mouse and experimental evidence; the proposed pathway is not an established clinical treatment target, and findings should not be extrapolated to intestinal disease.

stories.title: GPR55 structures reveal glycosylation-dependent reversal of a ligand's activity
stories.takeaway: Structural and functional experiments show that changing an extracellular GPR55 glycosylation site can switch a ligand from inverse agonism to agonism.
stories.what_happened: In Nature Communications on October 24, Claff and colleagues resolved inactive and active cryo-EM structures of the lipid-sensing receptor GPR55, developed an improved tool compound, and used mutagenesis, glycoproteomics and HDX-MS to investigate an activation mechanism unlike the canonical GPCR helix-VI movement.
stories.why_it_matters: Demonstrates why receptor glycosylation and structural context matter for chemical-probe interpretation and development of drugs targeting inflammation- and metabolism-associated signaling.
stories.caveat: Receptor structural and assay findings do not yet demonstrate efficacy in inflammatory disease or establish a clinically validated GPR55 therapeutic.

stories.title: Designed protein fiducials unlock cryo-EM views of difficult GPCR conformations
stories.takeaway: Generative protein design and ensemble prediction produced rigid fusion markers that enable cryo-EM analysis of small, flexible receptor states without conventional signaling partners.
stories.what_happened: Published October 24 in Nature Communications, Vo and colleagues determined inactive structures for four pharmacologically relevant GPCRs and engineered a beta2-adrenergic-receptor marker to examine intracellular rearrangements without G protein. The peer-reviewed publication follows a January 2026 preprint.
stories.why_it_matters: An enabling structural-bioengineering method that could expand access to receptor conformations important for mechanistic pharmacology and drug design.
stories.caveat: Demonstrated on selected receptors; performance and possible structural perturbations from fiducial fusions need case-specific assessment.

stories.title: Protein language models predict residue electrostatics directly from sequence
stories.takeaway: KaML-ESM models estimate protein residue pKa values from sequence, achieving approximately 0.5-unit RMSE on several native-protein benchmarks.
stories.what_happened: Shen and colleagues reported in Nature Communications on October 24 that ESM-based models trained with augmented pKa data predicted ionization behavior across benchmark proteins and enabled proteome-scale exploration of potential functional sites. Performance was poorer for buried engineered mutations.
stories.why_it_matters: Provides a computational route to prioritize protein-engineering hypotheses and explore catalytic mechanisms without requiring full atomistic simulations for every candidate.
stories.caveat: Generalization to unusual engineered variants is weaker; predictions are not a substitute for experimental validation or explicit physical modeling.
